title: Construction bids and asymmetric reliance
summary: The notes preserve the difference between protecting an opportunity to accept and binding both parties to performance.
notes: Baird and Drennan take different approaches to a general contractor’s use of a sub-bid. Drennan’s protection depends on justified reliance and prompt action, and it limits shopping or reopening the bargain. Holman rejects an automatic reciprocal duty based only on using the bid. Quality, reliability, and ordinary bid expenses feature in that account. The notes ask whether preparatory reliance before performance can satisfy § 87(2).

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 252–259. Open assigned page 252.
